title: Cutting and Drilling Clear Acrylic Sheet
author: Jakub Nedbal
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcueiwte

steps.title: Gather Materials and Drawing
steps.instruction: Collect a clear acrylic sheet, the technical drawing for the platform, a fine‑tip permanent marker, a ruler, and a carpenter square or protractor.

steps.title: Mark Outline and Hole Positions
steps.instruction: Using the marker, ruler and square, draw the platform outline on the acrylic sheet and mark the four mounting holes so that the spacing matches the drawing (287 mm and 191 mm between holes).

steps.title: Cut Acrylic with Hacksaw
steps.instruction: Secure the sheet and cut along the drawn outline with a hacksaw to obtain the desired platform shape.

steps.title: Deburr Edges with Sandpaper
steps.instruction: Smooth all cut edges using medium‑grit sandpaper (P80‑P180).

steps.title: Drill Mounting Holes
steps.instruction: Drill the four marked holes using a drill equipped with a 4 mm (5/32" or 3/16") multipurpose drill bit; plastic‑specific bits may be used if available to reduce cracking.

steps.title: Optional: Laser Cut Acrylic Sheet
steps.instruction: If a laser cutter is available, load the DXF file Orbital_Shaker_Clear_Acrylic_Sheet.dxf (derived from the Onshape model and edited in LibreCAD) into the cutter and follow the manufacturer’s operating instructions, ensuring only trained personnel operate the machine and all safety rules are observed.

description: Summary This document describes the steps to cut a clear acrylic sheet and drill holes into it to create a transparent shaking platform to place the culture flasks on. It offered a solution for laser cutting the sheet instead of doing it by hand. The sheet will be mounted on top of the orbital shaker, as explained in the next document on the final assembly.
